title: The Four Seasons: Summer, Concerto in G minor
hook: Heat that makes everything droop, a cuckoo, a shepherd afraid of the sky, and a hailstorm that flattens the corn.

painting.title: The Tempest
painting.pairingNote: A Venetian landscape under a heavy summer sky, with lightning flickering over the town while a young man with a staff and a seated woman wait below, the uneasy calm before the storm that Vivaldi’s sonnet describes.

facts: *Summer* is the second of the four concertos known as *The Four Seasons*, published in Amsterdam in 1725 as the first four of the twelve concertos of Vivaldi’s Op. 8, *Il cimento dell’armonia e dell’inventione* (“The contest between harmony and invention”). Like the others it was probably written some years earlier.

Each concerto comes with a sonnet, possibly by Vivaldi himself, and he printed its lines in the score next to the music that paints them. Summer’s sonnet is not about holidays. It is about the heat of the Italian countryside: people and flocks droop, the pines burn, birds sing, a cold north wind breaks in, and the shepherd weeps for fear of the storm. In the end the storm comes, with thunder and hail, and beats down the corn.

It is a concerto in the Baroque way: a refrain for the string band, the [[ritornello|ritornello]], alternates with passages for the solo violin, with the harpsichord and bass instruments, the [[continuo|continuo]], underneath. In *Summer* Vivaldi bends the plan: the first movement’s opening refrain is the heat itself, and a second, violent refrain, the north wind, arrives halfway through and has the last word.
It is the only one of the four concertos in which all three movements are in the same minor key, and the tension rises from start to finish.
bigPicture.inOneLine: heat, birdsong and a rising wind (I), a sleepless shepherd and distant thunder (II), the hailstorm (III).

movements.heading: Allegro non molto – Allegro
movements.summary: “Under the harsh season, set ablaze by the sun, man and flock languish.” The movement opens with weary, broken phrases separated by silences: the heat. Then the soloist bursts out as the cuckoo, followed by the turtledove and the goldfinch. Gentle breezes stir, the north wind suddenly sweeps in, and the shepherd weeps in fear of the storm.

mainIdeas.name: The heat
mainIdeas.description: short, sighing phrases in the strings, stopping and starting, as if too tired to go on. Vivaldi wrote “languor caused by the heat” over them.

mainIdeas.name: The birds
mainIdeas.description: fast, bright solo passages: the cuckoo, then the turtledove, then the goldfinch.

mainIdeas.name: The north wind
mainIdeas.description: a sudden, fierce rush of fast notes in the whole band.

stops.hear: Quiet, drooping phrases broken by silences; the music keeps stopping
stops.happening: “Languor caused by the heat”: the first [[ritornello|ritornello]]

stops.hear: The solo violin breaks out in fast, repeated two-note calls
A softer, slower solo with sighing notes
Quick, twittering trills high in the solo violin
Light, rocking figures in the violins
Suddenly the whole band rushes in, loud and fast
stops.happening: “But the north wind sweeps them aside”

stops.hear: A few quiet bars of the opening, then the solo violin, with little but the bass beneath, in a sad, halting line
stops.happening: The shepherd weeps, afraid of the storm

stops.label: Last 45 seconds
stops.hear: The rushing north wind again, to the end
stops.happening: The storm’s refrain closes the movement

notice: Listen to the silences at the start. Vivaldi makes the heat audible by letting the music run out of breath.

movements.heading: Adagio e piano – Presto e forte
movements.tempo: Adagio e piano – Presto e forte
movements.summary: The shepherd tries to rest, but “the fear of lightning and fierce thunder” and swarms of flies and gnats will not let him. The solo violin sings a slow, anxious line over the band’s restless buzzing, and every few bars the whole band breaks in with a short, loud burst of thunder.

mainIdeas.name: The shepherd
mainIdeas.description: a slow, sad melody in the solo violin.

mainIdeas.name: The flies
mainIdeas.description: short, nagging repeated notes in the violins of the band, soft and insistent.

mainIdeas.name: The thunder
mainIdeas.description: sudden, very fast and loud outbursts from everyone, then silence.

stops.hear: A slow, mournful solo line; underneath, the violins buzz softly with small repeated notes
stops.happening: The tired shepherd and the flies

stops.hear: A sudden, loud, fast outburst from the whole band, then quiet again
The pattern repeats: the lament, then thunder, a little more threatening each time

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The thunder breaks in once more before the last quiet phrase

notice: The contrast is written into the title: *Adagio e piano*, slow and soft, against *Presto e forte*, fast and loud. Count how many times the thunder interrupts.

movements.heading: Presto
movements.summary: “Alas, his fears were justified.” The storm breaks: thunder, lightning and hail that cut down the corn. Vivaldi builds the whole movement from storm sounds, furious repeated notes, scales plunging downwards and broken chords racing up the solo violin, with hardly a melody in sight.

mainIdeas.name: The storm
mainIdeas.description: fast, hammered repeated notes in the whole band, the sound of rain and hail.

mainIdeas.name: The lightning
mainIdeas.description: scales that tear downwards, in the band and the solo violin.

mainIdeas.name: The soloist’s flights
mainIdeas.description: rapid broken chords and runs, wilder each time.

stops.hear: The whole band explodes in furious repeated notes, then plunging scales
The solo violin races up and down in broken chords across its strings
The storm refrain again, in the band
For a moment something like a tune appears, then falls apart
The soloist’s fastest, most violent runs

stops.label: Last 20 seconds
stops.hear: The whole band, hammering to a sudden end
stops.happening: The storm has done its damage

notice: Listen for the repeated notes. Fast, even repetition on one pitch, the [[tremolo|tremolo]] of the strings, is Vivaldi’s sound for heavy rain and hail.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Simon Standage plays all four concertos with The English Concert on period instruments, and Trevor Pinnock directs from the harpsichord. *Summer* is tracks 4–6 of the Spotify album.

threads.title: The sonnet
threads.body: Every scene follows the poem in order: the heat, the cuckoo, the turtledove and goldfinch, the breezes, the north wind, the shepherd’s tears, the flies and thunder, the hailstorm.

threads.title: A storm that grows
threads.body: The north wind first appears in the middle of the first movement, thunder rumbles through the second, and the third is the storm itself.

threads.title: One key
threads.body: All three movements stay in G minor, which gives *Summer* a darker, more anxious colour than the other three seasons.
